title: Comparing Machine Learning Forecasting Models Based on Accuracy and Efficiency for Predicting Demand in a Food and Beverage Company
authors: Alunen, R.B.; Molina, C.F.; Quesada, R.F.; Reyes, C.N.; Jacob, D.
venue: Proceedings of the 6th African International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management
tldr: A comparative evaluation of Random Forest, XGBoost, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting for demand forecasting in a Philippine F&B company shows XGBoost with Random Search hyperparameter tuning achieves the best balance of accuracy and computational efficiency.
problem_and_motivation: The Philippine food and beverage industry struggles with accurate demand forecasting due to the inability of traditional methods to capture non-linear relationships and external factors such as holidays, weather, and macroeconomic conditions.
approach: Historical sales data from a Philippine restobar (2021–2024) covering three alcoholic beverage product categories were collected and merged with external predictors: unemployment rate, weather temperature, holiday indicators, and day of the week.
Pearson correlation-based feature selection removed factors with negligible correlation (less than ±0.3), producing two dataset variants: one with feature selection and one without.
Four machine learning algorithms were evaluated: Random Forest Regression, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and AdaBoost, sourced from Scikit-Learn in Python.
Two hyperparameter tuning methods—Grid Search and Random Search—were applied in separate trials with 10-fold cross-validation.
An 80/20 train-test split was used, and all combinations were evaluated using MAE, MSE, RMSE, R², and execution time.
ML models were compared against two traditional forecasting baselines: Multiple Linear Regression and Exponential Smoothing.
findings: XGBoost achieved the best overall balance of accuracy (R²=0.42) and computational efficiency (execution time=9.47s) across all products.
num: 31% higher adherence — not applicable; Feature selection improved computational efficiency but introduced slight accuracy reductions, with R² values remaining nearly identical across models.
Random Search outperformed Grid Search in both accuracy and execution time across all algorithms.
All ML models outperformed Multiple Linear Regression (MAE=10.44) and Exponential Smoothing (R²=0.07) in error minimization and predictive power.
For bucket of beers, XGBoost achieved the highest R² (0.52); for cocktails, Random Forest had the lowest MAE (3.09); for bottled beer, XGBoost and AdaBoost tied on R² (0.30).
Grid Search required significantly higher execution time (e.g., 390.43s for Random Forest) than Random Search (16.91s) with minimal accuracy differences.

key_equations.explanation: Mean Squared Error penalizes larger prediction errors by squaring differences.
Mean Absolute Error measures average magnitude of prediction errors.
Root Mean Squared Error is sensitive to outliers due to squared errors.
Coefficient of Determination measures proportion of variance explained by the model.

definitions.definition: Extreme Gradient Boosting, an ensemble method using sequentially boosted decision trees with regularization.
Adaptive Boosting, an algorithm that iteratively adjusts weights to focus on misclassified instances.
An ensemble of decision trees that aggregates predictions through bagging and random feature selection.
An ensemble method that builds trees sequentially, each correcting errors of the previous ones.
The process of identifying and removing irrelevant or redundant variables to improve model efficiency.
The process of optimizing model parameters that are not learned from data, such as tree depth or learning rate.
An exhaustive search over a specified parameter grid to find optimal hyperparameters.
A search strategy that samples hyperparameter combinations randomly from defined distributions.
Mean Absolute Error, the average of absolute differences between predicted and actual values.
Mean Squared Error, the average of squared differences between predicted and actual values.
Root Mean Squared Error, the square root of MSE, expressing error in the original unit.
Coefficient of Determination, measuring the proportion of variance in the dependent variable explained by the model.
Food and Beverage, the industry sector studied in this research.
Machine Learning, a subset of artificial intelligence focused on algorithmic learning from data.
Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average, a traditional time-series forecasting model.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a comparative evaluation of four machine learning algorithms for demand forecasting in the Philippine food and beverage sector.
directly_justifies: XGBoost combined with Random Search achieves the optimal balance between accuracy and computational efficiency for demand forecasting.
All ML models outperformed traditional methods (Multiple Linear Regression, Exponential Smoothing) in error minimization and R².
Feature selection using correlation improves computational efficiency but introduces slight reductions in forecast accuracy.
Random Search outperforms Grid Search in both accuracy and execution time across all evaluated algorithms.
External variables including macroeconomic indicators, weather, and holidays improve demand forecast accuracy when incorporated into ML models.
limits: Data from a single restobar in Quezon City limits generalizability to other regions and business types.
Overall R² values across all models remain below 0.52, indicating substantial unexplained variance in demand.
The study covers only three alcoholic beverage product categories, which may not represent broader F&B demand patterns.
No cross-validation across different time periods or geographic locations was performed to assess temporal robustness.

limitations: Data sourced from a single restobar in Quezon City limits generalizability to other regions and business types.
Overall R² values remain below 0.52 across all models, indicating substantial unexplained demand variance.
Only three alcoholic beverage product categories were evaluated, which may not represent broader F&B demand patterns.
No cross-validation across different time periods or geographic locations was conducted to assess temporal robustness.
The study does not address overfitting mitigation strategies or model performance degradation under distributional shift.
remember_this: XGBoost with Random Search tuning offers the best balance of accuracy and speed for F&B demand forecasting.
All ML models outperformed traditional forecasting methods in error minimization and predictive power.
Feature selection improves computational efficiency but introduces minor accuracy trade-offs.
External factors such as holidays, weather, and unemployment rate enhance demand forecast accuracy.
Overall R² values below 0.52 suggest significant unexplained variance across all evaluated models.
